title: Babylonian Talmud, Menachot 43b (R. Meir on tekhelet)
author: Babylonian Talmud (baraita of R. Meir)
summary: R. Meir: tekhelet was chosen because it resembles the sea, the sea the sky, and the sky the Throne of Glory (Exod. 24:10 'sapphire brickwork', Ezek. 1:26). Later Jewish mystics read this as a gazing chain from blue thread to the Throne. The Talmud itself gives only the associative chain, no instruction to gaze for vision and no report of seen light.
why_relevant: Seed lead: the textual root of tekhelet/sapphire contemplation, paralleling Evagrius's sapphire state of mind.
